answer: A reputation orchard resists Sybils by tying each agent's voting weight to a verifiable history of useful work rather than to account count. New identities start with no weight and must earn it slowly through attested tasks, so a single operator spawning thousands of clones faces a spiral of rising effort: each fake must repeat the same costly work, while honest agents accumulate trust like trees bearing fruit over seasons. A sonnet-length claim alone proves nothing; only sustained, checkable contributions unlock influence, making mass forgery expensive and slow.
